title: "A practical pattern for reproducible vignettes"
description: "A reusable structure for publishing analysis that readers can understand, inspect and reproduce."
date: 2026-09-22

---

Reproducibility is not achieved by adding a repository link at the end of an article. It starts with the way the analysis is organised and explained.

This is the default pattern I plan to use for longer technical pieces on this site.

## 1. Begin with a precise question

State what the analysis is trying to learn before introducing tools or data. A reader should be able to tell what would count as an answer—and what falls outside the scope.

## 2. Describe the evidence

Record each input’s source, coverage, retrieval date and licence. If a dataset changes over time, keep a stable snapshot or an exact version identifier.

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| Source | Publisher and canonical URL |
| Coverage | Geography, dates and population |
| Version | Release, retrieval date or checksum |
| Licence | Reuse terms and attribution |
| Known limits | Gaps, biases and measurement issues |

## 3. Keep transformations visible

Code should sit close to the claim it supports. Long setup sections can be folded by default, while decisive filters, joins and model choices remain easy to inspect.

```r
# A deliberately small example of an auditable transformation
daily_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(mode)) |>
  dplyr::count(date, mode, wt = trips, name = "trips")
```

## 4. Put interpretation beside output

A chart does not explain itself. Describe the dominant pattern, the comparison that matters and the uncertainty that should temper the conclusion. Interactive controls should reveal a meaningful choice—not decorate the page.

## 5. Make rerunning realistic

For R or Python work, pin dependencies with `renv` or a Python environment file. Quarto’s frozen computations can preserve article outputs between runs, while the environment files explain how to recreate them.

::: {.callout-note}
This site uses `freeze: auto`. When a computational article is rendered locally, its results can be committed in `_freeze/`; the publishing action can then rebuild the website without rerunning every historical analysis.
:::

## 6. Finish with boundaries

Say what the analysis cannot establish, what would change the conclusion, and what should be tried next. That final section is often more useful than a polished summary.

The template in this repository turns these headings into a practical starting point for the next vignette.
